Title: 'I should've been the one to resign,' says Hannah Yeoh
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: DAP Deputy National Publicity Secretary Hannah Yeoh has expressed regret over Anthony Loke's decision to resign as Transport Minister with immediate effect today.
Hannah, who is also minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories), said she should have been the one to step down, but Loke wanted to ensure that the party fulfilled its promises to the people and completed outstanding work.
"I should have been the one to resign today, but my secretary-general wanted us to fulfil all our promises to the people and complete the work that remains unfinished.
"In the end, he was the one who paid the price," she said in a Facebook post today.
Earlier, Loke, who is also DAP secretary-general, announced that his resignation as Transport minister would take effect immediately.
In a statement, Loke said the decision followed the Kuala Lumpur High Court's ruling today allowing Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
Media reports had previously said Loke had submitted his resignation letter as Transport minister to the prime minister on Sept 28.
Loke had announced his intention to resign following a DAP Central Executive Committee (CEC) meeting on Sept 19, amid the controversy surrounding the conditional pardon granted to Najib, the former prime minister.
However, Loke said other DAP ministers and deputy ministers would remain in the Unity Government.
Earlier, media reports said Najib would be transferred from Kajang Prison to his residence in Taman Duta today, with immediate effect, to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest in connection with the misappropriation of SRC International Sdn Bhd funds.
High Court judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin had set aside the order of discharge upon payment of a fine dated Nov 6.

Title: Expired import permit leads to seizure of 25 tonnes of frozen chicken
Article:
BUKIT KAYU HITAM: Nearly 25 tonnes of frozen chicken worth RM562,290 were seized by the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) after the importer was found to have submitted an expired import permit.
The seizure followed a physical inspection by MCBA officers at the Bilik Sejuk Beli, Block E1, Bukit Kayu Hitam Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security (ICQS) Complex, yesterday.
The inspection found that the frozen chicken products, categorised as 'Chicken Thigh & Leg Boneless Frozen', had been imported from Thailand.
Further checks revealed that the importer had submitted an import permit issued by the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Department (MAQIS) that had expired.
The consignment was seized under Section 11(1) of the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Act 2011 (Act 728).
The case was referred to MAQIS for further action.
MCBA Bukit Kayu Hitam commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Fauzi Mohd Yusof said the agency would not compromise on any violation of the law, particularly involving imports that failed to meet the stipulated requirements and regulations.
"Inspections and monitoring will continue to be stepped up to ensure all goods brought into the country are accompanied by valid permits and documents and comply with the laws in force," he said.

Title: Advancecon bags RM41.5mil Johor job
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Advancecon Holdings Bhd has secured a RM41.52 million contract for earthworks and infrastructure works at Southern Ibrahim Technopolis (IBTEC) in Kulai, Johor.
The project, undertaken by subsidiary Advancecon Infra Sdn Bhd, is expected to take 19 months to complete.
It is scheduled for completion on June 3, 2028.
The latest award marks the company's third contract from JLG Technopark for work at IBTEC.
Advancecon said the development is expected to contribute to strengthening Johor's position as a regional investment destination.
The latest win will further replenish Advancecon's outstanding order book, supporting its construction pipeline and providing additional earnings visibility over the contract period.
Advancecon managing director Phum Boon Eng said the contract reflects its technical capabilities and track record in delivering large-scale earthworks and infrastructure projects.
"Johor continues to present opportunities for industrial and infrastructure development, supported by ongoing investments in manufacturing, technology and other high-value industries.
"With IBTEC emerging as an important industrial and technology hub, we are pleased to contribute our expertise towards supporting its progressive development," she added.

Title: Home Ministry ready to implement Najib's house arrest order
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Home Ministry is ready to implement the High Court's decision ordering former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his six-year prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the ministry had always respected and upheld the royal pardon granted by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim, in accordance with the powers vested in His Majesty under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution.
"The High Court today ordered that the Order of Discharge on Payment of Fine dated Nov 6 be set aside and replaced with a Conditional Pardon Order, requiring the accused to serve the remainder of his six-year prison sentence under house arrest at No. 11, Jalan Langgak Duta, Taman Duta, Kuala Lumpur.
"Every decision made through constitutional channels must be respected and implemented in accordance with the law," he said in a statement today.
Saifuddin Nasution said the delay in implementation was due to legal questions surrounding the interpretation of the Conditional Pardon Order and the legal implications of the release order dated Nov 6, particularly regarding the enforcement of the remaining sentence through house arrest.
"The High Court's decision today has clarified these questions," he said.
He said the ministry respected the Attorney General's Chambers' position that the legal questions needed to be clarified through judicial proceedings to ensure that every government action had a clear, proper and valid legal basis.
"As home minister, I emphasise that the responsibility of the Home Ministry and the Prisons Department is to ensure that every decision concerning the enforcement of sentences and detention is carried out in accordance with the law and valid court orders," he said.
Saifuddin Nasution said the case was a high-profile matter with significant political implications and public perceptions, requiring all parties to handle it with maturity and responsibility.
He also cautioned against allowing political controversies to undermine public confidence in national institutions.
"The government will continue to defend the position and role of the Malay Rulers within the framework of the constitutional monarchy while upholding the supremacy of the Constitution, the rule of law and judicial independence. These principles complement one another and form the foundation of national stability," he said.
The High Court today ordered Najib, 73, to serve the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case under house arrest at his residence, with immediate effect.
Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin made the ruling after setting aside an order issued against Najib by the High Court Criminal Registry on Nov 6.
Under the new order, Najib will remain under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, before returning to Kajang Prison on Aug 24, 2028, to serve his prison sentence in connection with the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) case.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Jati Tinggi unit wins RM33.09mil data centre power infrastructure works
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Jati Tinggi Group Bhd's wholly owned subsidiary, Jati Tinggi Holding Sdn Bhd, has secured a RM33.09 million contract for power infrastructure works to support a data centre in Gerbil, Negeri Sembilan.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, it said the contract involves the supply, design, installation, testing and commissioning of two circuits of 275 kilovolt power cables connecting the transition yard to the data centre substation.
It also covers the construction of a transition yard, overhead line T-off works and related secondary system modifications to support the data centre's interim power supply infrastructure requirements.
"The contract shall be for a period of nine months effective from the notice to start work," it said.

Title: Sunway REIT's Q3 net profit falls to RM116.17mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Real Estate Investment Trust (Reit) today reported a lower net profit of RM116.17 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 2026) compared to RM121.85 a year earlier.
Its revenue also eased by 1.4 per cent to RM232.31 million from RM236.43 million in the same quarter last year, the real estate investment trust said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia.
Sunway Reit Management Sdn Bhd, the manager of Sunway Reit, said the decline in revenue was mainly due to the disposal of Sunway university and college campus in September 2025 in line with its asset recycling strategy, resulting in a one-off gain on disposal of RM25.6 million in Q3 2025.
For the nine-month period ended Sept 30, 2026, net profit dropped to RM331.80 million from RM344.04 million in last year's corresponding period.
Revenue, however, grew to RM675.67 million from RM666.69 million previously, driven by a stronger contribution of RM43.1 million from the retail segment, more than offsetting the absence of RM29.3 million in revenue contribution from Sunway university and college campus.
Sunway Reit Management chief executive officer Derek Teh Wan Wei said Sunway Reit continued to demonstrate the resilience and quality of its diversified portfolio in Q3 2026.
He said the retail segment remained the key growth driver, supported by strong shopper traffic, healthy tenant sales, positive rental reversions and sustained contributions from our retail assets.
Teh said the office segment also delivered improved performance on the back of stronger occupancy and leasing momentum, while the hotel segment experienced temporary headwinds arising from the ongoing conflicts in Middle East and haze-related disruptions in the Klang Valley.
"Looking ahead, we remain cautiously optimistic about Sunway Reit's overall prospects for the remainder of 2026.
"The retail segment is expected to sustain its growth momentum, supported by resilient consumer spending, strong occupancy levels and positive rental reversions, while the office and industrial segments are poised to benefit further from continued leasing momentum and improving occupancy," he said.
For the hotel segment, Teh said, Sunway Reit would remain focused on strengthening performance through proactive marketing and pricing strategies, while enhancing demand across banqueting and MICE activities.
"Moving forward, we will continue to prioritise proactive asset management, operational efficiency and sustainable growth to enhance portfolio resilience and deliver long-term value to our unitholders," he said.
Sunway Reit owns a diversified portfolio of 28 properties comprising 14 retail properties, six hotels, five offices and three industrial properties, with a combined property value of RM10.3 billion.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit ends higher against US dollar amid hopes of de-escalation in US-Iran conflict
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended marginally higher against the US dollar on Tuesday, supported by improving market sentiment amid expectations of a de-escalation of the US-Iran conflict.
At 6pm, the local currency rose to 4.0540/0580 versus the greenback from Friday's close of 4.0565/0610.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said this came as US President Donald Trump indicated that further strikes against Iran were unnecessary.
"The conclusion of the US midterm elections last week could also have a significant impact on the current administration's policies.
"The ringgit traded mostly within a narrow range against the US dollar today, fluctuating between RM4.0510 and RM4.0590. At 5.05 pm, the ringgit stood at RM4.0547, appreciating by 0.11 per cent from Friday's close," he told Bernama.
Mohd Afzanizam said the trend was in tandem with the decline in the US Dollar Index, which fell by 0.14 per cent to 101.51, while Brent crude oil prices continued their downward trend to US$89.89 per barrel.
"For now, expectations of a de-escalation of the war in Iran have been instrumental in driving market sentiment," he added.
The ringgit traded lower against a basket of major currencies.
It eased against the Japanese yen to 2.5642/5669 from 2.5616/5646, depreciated vis-a-vis the euro to 4.5514/5559 from 4.5315/5365 and weakened against the British pound to 5.4425/4479 from 5.4304/4365 at Friday's close.
The ringgit also traded lower against its Asean peers.
It slid against the Singapore dollar to 3.1726/1758 from 3.1657/1694, slipped against the Thai baht to 12.1337/1497 from 12.0898/1105, eased vis-a-vis the Indonesian rupiah to 224.4/224.7 from 224.2/224.6 and weakened against the Philippine peso to 6.44/6.45 from 6.43/6.44 previously.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid: BN can do better than Anwar-led government
Article:
MELAKA: Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi says the coalition can deliver an even better government than the current administration led by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, which he acknowledged had performed well and achieved much.
He said the administration had implemented various positive measures, but BN was determined to build on those achievements and deliver even better results.
"We want to acknowledge that the government under the leadership of the prime minister is a good government. It has done well and accomplished many things.
"I repeat, this is a good government. Let me say it again, a good government.
"But, if we are given the mandate, we will do even better. However, we will have to wait and see," he said.
Zahid, who is also deputy prime minister, was speaking at a gathering with Melaka Community Development Department (Kemas) personnel.
Also present were Rural and Regional Development Ministry deputy secretary-general (policy) Datuk Abdul Kahar Abdullah, Melaka senior executive councillor Datuk Rais Yasin and Kemas director-general Datuk Mohd Hanafiah Man.
Zahid also called on voters to give BN a stronger mandate in the Melaka election, setting a target of winning more than the 21 state seats previously secured by the coalition.
"Imagine if we could turn more than 21 seats in Melaka blue.
"Make sure that this Saturday, we turn Melaka blue again with an even bigger number of seats.
"On Nov 14, make sure Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh continues to lead Melaka as its chief minister," he said.
He said political stability was crucial to ensuring the smooth administration of the Melaka government.
Zahid also reminded BN members not to focus solely on winning the state election but to prepare for the next general election by reclaiming parliamentary seats in Melaka.
"Remember, this is a state election. After this comes the general election.
"Our focus must not be limited to the state election. We must ensure that the parliamentary constituencies we contest in Melaka do not suffer the same fate as before.
"We must reclaim the parliamentary seats in Melaka," he said.
Zahid also expressed hope that renewed political cooperation between BN and Perikatan Nasional (PN) would further strengthen the coalition's chances of victory.
"Hopefully, the spirit and momentum of our previous victories, coupled with the support of our friends, including those with whom we have renewed longstanding ties, will help secure victory for us," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid expresses gratitude over court ruling on Najib's house arrest
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has expressed gratitude following the High Court's decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest with immediate effect.
The deputy prime minister, who is also Umno president, said the decision was significant for Umno and Barisan Nasional leaders and members, as well as those who had been praying for Najib to be reunited with his family.
"We also wish to express our deepest gratitude to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, who chaired the Pardons Board and decided that Najib could serve the remainder of his sentence at home.
"I would also like to thank the entire Umno leadership at all levels, party members and Malaysians who contributed to the public fundraising campaign, which raised the RM50 million needed to pay the fine imposed on him," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after launching the RISDA Smallholders' Prosperity Programme and Melaka State Open Day 2026 at Universiti Kolej Agrosains Malaysia in Ayer Pa'abas here today.
Zahid hoped the latest development would put an end to the prolonged controversy surrounding the implementation of the royal addendum order allowing Najib to serve his sentence under house arrest.
He said all parties, including legal practitioners and institutions responsible for administering the law, should respect the powers vested in the royal institution under the Federal Constitution.
"Hopefully, what has happened and is happening will serve as a lesson to all of us, whether we are legal practitioners or those responsible for upholding the law, to comply with the decrees and powers of His Majesty the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
"This is because, in law, the provisions enshrined in the Constitution are principles that must be upheld," he said.
Zahid also prayed that all of Najib's affairs would be made easier and that the former prime minister would be able to enjoy a peaceful life with his family.
Earlier today, the High Court set aside a release order dated Nov 6 and replaced it with a new order allowing Najib, 73, to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest at Jalan Langgak Duta, Kuala Lumpur, until Aug 23, 2028.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang cops told to step up preparations for monsoon disasters
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Police departments and district headquarters across Penang have been ordered to strengthen logistical and operational preparations ahead of anticipated disasters during the northeast monsoon.
Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim said personnel deployment, operational assets and coordination with other agencies must be stepped up immediately to ensure swift responses.
"All departments and districts must reinforce preparations in terms of personnel deployment, operational assets and coordination with relevant agencies.
"This is vital to ensure rapid and effective action should any disaster occur," he said at the Penang police contingent's monthly assembly at the state police headquarters today.
Lim said public safety remained the priority, stressing the need for close cooperation between the police and other disaster relief agencies throughout the monsoon period.
On other matters, Lim said integrity, discipline and professionalism remained essential among all personnel.
He warned that misconduct, abuse of power and extortion would not be tolerated, urging personnel to uphold public trust through transparent service.
The monthly assembly, organised by the contingent's Special Branch, also saw 19 senior police officers confirmed in their promotions to the rank of deputy superintendent of police (DSP).
Another 34 personnel received certificates of appreciation for their dedication and contributions to crime-fighting efforts across the state.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid wishes Loke 'all the best'
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has described Anthony Loke as a principled leader who stands by his convictions.
Commenting on the DAP secretary-general's resignation as transport minister, Zahid said he respected the Seremban member of Parliament's decision and appreciated his service and cooperation as a cabinet member.
"I have read his statement on his resignation.
"He is a principled person who stands by his principles. I would like to thank him for his service as a member of the cabinet," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after officiating at the RISDA Smallholders' Prosperity Programme and Melaka State Open Day 2026 at Universiti Kolej Agrosains Malaysia (UCAM) in Ayer Pa'abas here today.
Zahid said Loke's departure would be felt by other cabinet members, particularly as he was a senior member of the unity government Cabinet.
"He sits to my right at every cabinet meeting, so his absence will certainly be felt at the next meeting. I wish him all the best outside the cabinet," he said.
Earlier, Loke announced that
his resignation as transport minister would take effect immediately,
following the Kuala Lumpur High Court's decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
The resignation was in line with DAP's position against a conditional pardon for Najib, although the party respected the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's power and prerogative in matters of pardons.
Loke had submitted his resignation letter to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Sept 28, but was asked to continue serving while matters relating to Najib's house arrest were being resolved.
He also assured that he would provide full cooperation to ensure a smooth transition at the Transport Ministry, with the implementation of its policies and projects continuing as planned.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Foreign buying lifts bond holdings by RM7.2bil to RM325.5bil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Foreign holdings of Malaysian bonds posted a strong inflow in October, signalling confidence in Malaysia's economic fundamentals.
In its October fixed income review, MBSB Research said the outstanding value moved higher by RM7.2 billion to RM325.5 billion.
"Foreign holdings saw a significant increase in the final week of October, reaching a record high.
"We estimate that the share of foreign holdings in total outstanding government debt edged higher to 21 per cent," it said.
The firm said the US Treasury (UST) yield curve experienced a flattening last month, averaging around 5.12 per cent on the back of heightened geopolitical risk and expectations for a delayed rate hike.
In early October, a sharp sell-off temporarily pushed the 10-year UST yield to a multi-decade high of 5.342 per cent.
However, yields steadily eased lower through the remainder of the month.
Downward momentum accelerated following the announcement made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) announcement, where it voted 10–2 to hold the fed funds target rate steady at 3.75 per cent–4.00 per cent.
"The split decision signalled a hawkish hold, reinforcing the possibility of further monetary tightening, although the US Federal Reserve (Fed) opted to assess incoming economic data before its next policy decision.
"Nevertheless, market expectations remain tilted toward a potential 25 basis points (bps) rate hike at the upcoming FOMC meeting in December," said the firm.
Back home, the Malaysian government securities (MGS) yield curve closed lower last month, across all tenors, as most of the decline was towards the longer end of the curve, indicating a bull flattening of the yield curve.
The yield curve initially declined during the early part of the month, but later closed relatively higher, broadly tracking the movement of the UST yields.
The MGS 10-year yield traded between 3.799 per cent and 4.028 per cent last month, while the UST 10-year yield traded lower within the range of 4.930 per cent to 5.307 per cent.
"Concurrently, we expect the continuous hawkish outlook for the US fed funds rate has led markets to price in a hawkish and 'higher-for-longer' policy stance.
"Investors anticipate a 25bps rate hike at the upcoming FOMC meeting in December.
"On that note, we expect MGS yields will continue to mirror the movement in UST yields in the short- to medium-term, subject to inflationary risk and the Middle East conflicts, on top of the possibility of a further rate hike by the FOMC."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Big Caring IPO final price at RM1.08, oversubscribed 4.31 times
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Big Caring Group Bhd's initial public offering (IPO) has been priced at RM1.08 per share, with its public tranche oversubscribed 4.31 times ahead of its listing on Bursa Malaysia's Main Market.
The final retail price of RM1.08 matches the institutional price determined through the bookbuilding process, with no refund required for successful retail applicants.
Malaysian Issuing House Sdn Bhd said the public portion, comprising 147.64 million shares, received 29,474 applications for 783.75 million shares.
The Bumiputera portion attracted 7,266 applications for 142.85 million shares, representing an oversubscription rate of 0.94 times.
Meanwhile, the other Malaysian public portion received 22,208 applications for 640.9 million shares, translating into an oversubscription rate of 7.68 times.
The 120 million shares allocated to eligible directors, employees and other contributors to the group were fully subscribed after applying the relevant clawback and reallocation provisions.
The institutional offering of 1.61 billion shares to Malaysian and foreign institutional and selected investors was also fully subscribed.
Of the institutional offering, 19 cornerstone investors subscribed for 41.2 per cent.
Big Caring's IPO involves up to 1.88 billion shares, comprising an offer for sale of 1.29 billion existing shares and a public issue of 590.55 million new shares.
It is poised to become Malaysia's second-largest IPO of 2026 by market capitalisation, with a valuation of about RM8 billion ahead of its Main Market debut on Nov 19.
At that valuation, Big Caring will rank behind Sunway Healthcare Holdings Bhd, which made its market debut in March with an IPO valuation of RM16.68 billion.
It will also be more than three times the size of MTT Shipping and Logistics Bhd, which was valued at RM2.58 billion when it listed in April.
The notices of allotment will be mailed to successful applicants by Nov 18.
Maybank Investment Bank Bhd and RHB Investment Bank Bhd are the joint principal advisers, joint global coordinators, joint bookrunners, joint managing underwriters and joint underwriters for the IPO.
AmInvestment Bank Bhd is also a joint principal adviser, joint global coordinator, joint bookrunner and joint underwriter.
UBS Securities Malaysia Sdn Bhd and UBS AG, Singapore Branch are joint global coordinators and joint bookrunners.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Legal questions delayed Najib's house arrest implementation, says Saifuddin
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Legal questions over the interpretation of the conditional pardon order and a subsequent discharge order had delayed the implementation of Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
Responding to the High Court's decision today allowing the former prime minister to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest, Saifuddin said the ruling had clarified the legal issues.
He said questions surrounding the conditional pardon order and the Nov 6 discharge order, particularly the provision for house arrest, had held up its implementation.
Saifuddin said the ministry was now ready to implement the court's decision to set aside the Nov 6 order for Najib's discharge upon payment of a fine and allow him to serve the remainder of his six-year sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
"In this regard, the ministry respects the Attorney-General's Chambers' position that these questions should be clarified through judicial proceedings.
"This approach is important to ensure that every government action has a clear, orderly and lawful legal basis," he said.
He said the ministry and the Prisons Department would ensure that all decisions on the implementation of sentences and detention complied with the law and valid court orders.
"The ministry has always respected and upheld royal pardon decisions granted by His Majesty the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, in accordance with the powers vested under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution.
"Every decision made through constitutional channels must be respected and implemented in accordance with the law," he said.
Article 42 of the Federal Constitution provides for the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites and remissions, as well as to suspend or commute sentences.
Saifuddin described the case as high-profile, with significant political implications and public interest, and urged all parties to handle it responsibly.
He said political polemics should not undermine public confidence in the country's institutions.
"The government will continue to uphold the position and role of the Malay Rulers within the framework of a constitutional monarchy, while safeguarding the supremacy of the Constitution, the rule of law and the independence of the judiciary.
"These principles complement one another and form the foundation of the country's stability," he said.

Title: Nepal flood victims' families may wait up to a year for death certificates
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Families of Malaysians missing in the Nepal floods could face another three to 12 months, or longer, to obtain certificates of presumption of death, Malaysia Solidarity Families in Hope (Masfih) said.
Its coordinator and spokesman, Dr R Manivannan, said the process could be prolonged by uncertainty over whether documents issued by Nepal would be recognised directly by Malaysia or require further legal procedures.
He said it remained unclear whether families could submit the Nepali documents directly to the National Registration Department (NRD), or whether they would first need a court order or further assessment.
"We believe this matter could drag on for three to nine months, even 12 months more," he told reporters after a briefing with the Raja Puan Muda of Kedah, Che Puan Muda Zaheeda Mohamad Ariff, at Istana Darul Aman today.
Manivannan said families would still need to settle estate matters through probate or Letters of Administration after the NRD issued the certificates, while Muslim families would also have to go through the faraid inheritance process.
Citing the MH370 tragedy in 2014, he said families had waited nearly 2 years for death certificates after the search and rescue operation was called off on Jan 29, 2015.
He said the NRD announced on Jan 30, 2015, that families could apply for death certificates after obtaining a court order, but the documents were only issued in December 2016.
Manivannan said Masfih hoped the same delays would not recur, adding that the Raja Puan Muda had expressed interest in exploring ways to expedite the process.
Masfih
had earlier questioned
whether the required document was a Certificate of Presumed Death or a standard Death Certificate under Nepal's revised disaster ordinance.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Najib arrives at Kajang Prison ahead of transfer to Taman Duta home
Article:
KAJANG: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak arrived at Kajang Prison at 6.14pm for final preparations before being transferred to his residence to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
A convoy of five vehicles carrying Najib was seen entering the prison compound.
He is expected to be taken from the prison to his residence in Jalan Langgak Duta, Taman Duta, Kuala Lumpur, where he will serve the remainder of his sentence.
Earlier, Najib's lawyer, Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah, said Najib was expected to begin serving his sentence at home after stopping at
Kajang Prison.
This follows the High Court's decision to set aside the Nov 6 order for discharge upon payment of a fine and replace it with an order requiring Najib to serve his sentence under house arrest.
High Court judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin
ordered Najib
to serve the remainder of his reduced six-year prison term at his residence in Jalan Langgak Duta until Aug 23, 2028, in accordance with the conditional royal pardon granted on Sept 18.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Najib posts 'Alhamdulillah' after court orders house arrest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Najib Razak has posted a brief "Alhamdulillah" message on his Facebook page following the High Court's order allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest.
The former prime minister shared the one-word post after High Court judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin today ordered him to serve the remainder of his reduced six-year prison term at his
Taman Duta residence
until Aug 23, 2028.
Earlier, Aslam set aside the Nov 6 order of discharge on payment of fine and replaced it in full with today's order, in accordance with the conditional royal pardon granted on Sept 18.
The order takes effect immediately.
Najib's lawyer, Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah, said Najib was expected to begin serving his sentence at home after stopping at
Kajang Prison.
Shafee said prison officers would read out the house arrest conditions to Najib at the prison before taking him to his Taman Duta residence.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bajau Sama oral art maestro named National Living Heritage Figure
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Bajau Sama's traditional oral art has earned national recognition, with its leading practitioner, Masruh Siadik, named a National Living Heritage Figure (WAKOH) 2026.
Masruh was recognised in the Language and Literature Arts category for his contributions to preserving, developing and promoting Isun-Isun, a traditional art form practised by the Bajau Sama and Iranun communities in Kota Belud.
"Isun-Isun combines oral poetry and music through exchanges of pantun between male and female singers, accompanied by a traditional violin.
"The art form is traditionally performed at weddings, childbirth celebrations, vow-fulfilment ceremonies and cultural events, including the Kota Belud Tamu Besar and Regatta Lepa," according to a statement by the Sabah National Department for Culture and Arts (JKKN).
As a maestro and leading authority on the art form, Masruh leads performances, arranges the sequence of pantun and accompanies singers on the traditional violin.
His efforts to promote Isun-Isun beyond Sabah include representing the Sabah Sports and Cultural Board at the National Dance Festival in Kuala Lumpur and representing Malaysia at the Culture Art and Tourism Foundation Festival in Bursa, Türkiye.
He is also an important source of knowledge for cultural researchers and institutions, including JKKN, as well as younger generations interested in traditional violin music and Bajau oral literature.
WAKOH is among the country's highest honours for individuals who have made significant contributions to safeguarding intangible cultural heritage.
Since the National Heritage Act 2005 (Act 645) came into force, 27 cultural practitioners from various ethnic, cultural and religious backgrounds have been recognised as National Living Heritage Figures.
Other WAKOH 2026 recipients include Che Mat Jusoh, recognised for nearly 58 years of preserving Kelantanese Mak Yong and Wayang Kulit; Che Mohd Nasir Yusoff, better known as Pak Nasir, for his expertise in Kelantanese Wayang Kulit; Toh Ai Hwa, for preserving Teochew iron-rod puppet performances in Penang for more than six decades; and Siow Ho Phiew, for lion-head puppet making and lion dance.
Sarawak practitioners Bangie Anak Embol, Salbiah Muhi and Razali Yu were also recognised for their expertise in Pua Kumbu weaving and Keringkam embroidery.

Title: Raja Puan Muda of Kedah meets families of Malaysians missing in Nepal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Families of Malaysians missing in the Nepal floods have sought clarification on delayed financial assistance and other benefits during an audience with the Raja Puan Muda of Kedah, Che Puan Muda Zaheeda Mohamad Ariff.
Malaysia Solidarity Families in Hope (MASFIH) coordinator and spokesperson Dr R. Manivannan said the families also sought updates on the disbursement of benefits from the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso).
On Oct 30, MASFIH said Perkeso payments to the next of kin of Malaysians affected by the Nepal-Tibet flood tragedy were expected to be
disbursed on Nov 4.
However, Manivannan said only the RM3,000 assistance had reached the 28 affected families so far, while pension payments and other benefits remained outstanding.
He said the families were also awaiting the RM10,000 one-off government assistance, which had been announced but not yet disbursed.
"We have a six-month debt moratorium, but families still have daily living expenses to meet, while salaries and other sources of income have stopped.
"We hope the assistance can be channelled as soon as possible, as only then will it help the families," he told reporters at Istana Darul Aman.
He said most affected households were from the B40 and M40 income groups, adding that some might turn to third-party lenders if the assistance continued to be delayed.
The briefing, held on the 77th day since the tragedy, also covered the progress of search, rescue and recovery operations, the families' welfare needs, as well as legal and documentation challenges.
Manivannan said the Raja Puan Muda had taken note of the difficulties families faced in obtaining certificates of presumption of death and offered to seek legal assistance through her contacts in the legal fraternity.
He said she, in her capacity as patron of the Malaysian Mental Health Association (MMHA), had also invited its executive director, Fazlin Badri Alyeope, to explore emotional and psychological support for the affected families.
To date, 54 Malaysians remain unaccounted for following flash floods in Rasuwagadhi, Nepal, on Aug 26.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dutch Lady buys 35pct stake in Jemaluang Dairy from Kulim
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Dutch Lady Milk Industries Bhd has agreed to buy a 35 per cent stake in Johor-based integrated dairy business Jemaluang Dairy Valley Sdn Bhd from Kulim (Malaysia) Bhd.
The completion of the proposed acquisition remains subject to conditions under the share sale agreement, including third-party approvals.
Upon completion, Dutch Lady Malaysia will join Kulim, a wholly owned subsidiary of Johor Corporation (JCorp), and A2 Fresh Holdings Sdn Bhd (A2F), a subsidiary of Rhone Ma Holdings Bhd, as shareholders in Jemaluang Dairy.
Dutch Lady Malaysia said the investment will strengthen its presence in the domestic fresh milk segment as the country seeks to expand local dairy production and improve food security.
Managing director Veronika Utami said the company saw opportunities to build on its position in the Malaysian market as consumer preferences continued to evolve.
"We look forward to working with Kulim and A2F to support Jemaluang Dairy's continued development, while exploring how our market knowledge and consumer insights can help us respond to changing needs and bring more choices to Malaysian consumers," she said.
JCorp president and chief executive Datuk Syed Mohamed Syed Ibrahim said the partnership would bring together complementary capabilities across the dairy value chain.
"A competitive dairy industry needs strong local production, industry expertise, reliable operations and market access across its value chain.
"Through Kulim, we have helped lay the foundation at Jemaluang Dairy. This partnership with Dutch Lady Malaysia brings complementary capabilities to unlock its long-term commercial potential," he said.
Jemaluang Dairy will continue operating under its existing management, with the three shareholders working under agreed governance arrangements to develop the business and explore opportunities in Malaysia's dairy market.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Russia and Ukraine hold first peace talks for nine months, gaps have narrowed
Article:
ABU DHABI: Russian and Ukrainian officials met in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday for their first US-brokered talks since February, after President Donald Trump suggested last week that a broad deal was possible on ending the war in Ukraine and guaranteeing security in Europe.
US envoy Jared Kushner told delegates that recent contacts with both sides had "really identified, narrowed the gaps", and that Trump was committed to achieving peace.
"He really has asked us to put extra effort into trying to find a solution that hopefully ends the war but also leaves both sides in a much stronger position to start pursuing the full potential of what their two amazing countries have the ability to reach," Kushner said at the start of the meeting.
But more than 4-1/2 years after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, and with Russian forces holding about a fifth of the country, Moscow and Kyiv remain far apart - despite Trump's optimism - on terms for a possible settlement.
Ukraine's chief delegate, Rustem Umerov, said in his opening remarks that Kyiv was focused on achieving security guarantees and a lasting peace.
[[nid:1574838]]
Russian delegation chief Vladimir Medinsky said Moscow hoped for progress towards peace in the interest of the peoples of both countries.
The new American drive for a deal has galvanised European officials into pushing for a place at the table to seek an end to the continent's deadliest conflict since World War Two.
Before the start of the main meeting, the Ukrainians met separately with European, Nato and EU representatives and the two American envoys, Kushner and Steve Witkoff.
France said there could be no lasting peace in Ukraine without addressing European security, and that this required the involvement of the Europeans.
Russia had made clear it did not see a place for Europeans at the meeting with the Ukrainians and Americans.
On the eve of the talks, Trump said Washington was seeing a "very strong inclination" towards ending the war, and that both sides were "tired of fighting."
After meeting privately with Russian President Vladimir Putin's envoy last week at the White House, Trump predicted that a peace deal could emerge soon.
Trump has frequently said an agreement was close, without a deal emerging.
However, negotiations have picked up again in recent weeks after months in which Washington's attention was focused on the war in Iran.
Publicly, there has been no sign that Putin is willing to drop his insistence that Ukraine surrender the entire eastern region of Donbas before a peace deal can be struck.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has refused to hand over land that his forces have died defending.
Russian front-line advances have slowed to a virtual halt this year but Moscow has been pounding Ukrainian cities and energy facilities, while Ukraine has stepped up attacks on oil refineries and other infrastructure deep inside Russia.
[[nid:1574837]]
A source in the Russian delegation said Russia believed the main thrust of the talks would be trying to hammer out the key elements of a new post-war security framework for Europe.
On the eve of the negotiations, Zelenskyy said Ukraine's leverage in the talks was increasing as a result of its recent battlefield performance, which has included retaking some territory in Donetsk, a coal-mining area of the Donbas.
"Ukrainian forces are currently genuinely strengthening Ukraine's negotiating position," Zelenskyy said in his nightly video address on Monday.
He said Russia was suffering "record losses" — an assertion disputed by Moscow — and urged Washington to convince the Kremlin to end the war.
US negotiators believe that Zelenskyy and Putin may be willing to strike a compromise on the vital question of territory, each ceding a little, a US official told Reuters.
Under the proposed deal, Ukraine would get an end to the war, security guarantees and a roadmap to accession to the EU.
A senior Ukrainian official strongly denied that the government would consider any such concessions.
The issue of territory could be discussed only at a leaders' level and only in the context of appropriate security guarantees for Ukraine, the official said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian sukuk remains most liquid: Fitch
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian ringgit-denominated sukuk have maintained liquidity above pre-Iran conflict levels, outperforming the broader global sukuk market amid continued geopolitical uncertainty, according to Fitch Ratings.
Fitch said Malaysian sukuk were among the most liquid in its coverage, alongside those from Hong Kong, supranational issuers and Indonesia, with average liquidity scores across these markets ranging between 69 and 95.
The firm said the average liquidity across all rated sukuk stood at 62 in early November, unchanged from Oct 1 but below the 68 recorded on Jan 30.
The overall score recovered about 12 per cent from 55 in March.
About 69 per cent of Fitch-rated sukuk had liquidity scores above 50 as at Nov 2, compared with a low of 64 per cent in March and 81 per cent in January.
"Malaysian ringgit sukuk remained the most liquid, continuing to trade above pre-conflict liquidity levels.
"The liquidity score of euro-denominated sukuk rose to about 81. In the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), local-currency sukuk were more liquid than bonds.
"By tenor, sukuk with maturities of under a year and those with maturities of 10 years or more were the most liquid," it said.
Among GCC markets, sukuk from Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Kuwait recorded an average liquidity score of about 57.
Although liquidity in these markets was briefly affected by Houthi attacks in late October, it has since rebounded, but remains below January's level.
Fitch expects sukuk liquidity to remain sensitive to geopolitical tensions, heightened interest rates, and capital reallocation from emerging markets to developed markets.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar shares light-hearted moment with Trevor Noah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today received a visit from South African comedian Trevor Noah ahead of his show tonight.
Anwar said they discussed politics, humour and various other topics during a meeting filled with laughter.
In a Facebook post, he said he had also offered Noah some advice on the jokes he could deliver on stage.
"It was a pleasure to receive a visit from Trevor Noah today.
"We managed to talk about politics, humour and all sorts of stories interspersed with laughter," he said.
Anwar added that he had shared some suggestions for the comedian's performance.
"I also managed to pass on some guidance on jokes that can be brought to the stage tonight. Hope no one gets offended!" he said.
He ended his post with a light-hearted assurance to Noah.
"Anyway, don't worry Trevor, if anything happens tonight, we'll all crowdfund together!" he said.
The remark comes days after Umno settled the RM50 million fine imposed on
former
prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak through the Najib Razak Solidarity Fund, a crowdfunding initiative launched in September.
Noah made his Malaysian
debut
at Idea Live Arena in Petaling Jaya on Nov 9.

Title: Lianson adds DP2 heavy-lift vessel
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Lianson Fleet Group Bhd (LFG) has unveiled the LFG Hercules, the first Malaysian-flagged dynamic positioning class 2 (DP2) offshore heavy-lift vessel, following its acquisition in October.
The vessel was unveiled at a naming ceremony in Melaka officiated by Transport Ministry secretary-general Datuk Seri Jana Santhiran Muniayan.
With a lifting capacity of up to 4,000 metric tonnes, the vessel is designed to support large-scale offshore operations, including decommissioning, heavy-lift installation and construction, as well as renewable energy infrastructure projects.
Its DP2 system allows the vessel to maintain its position during complex offshore operations, enabling Lianson to pursue higher-value and more technically demanding projects in the region.
Jana Santhiran said the vessel's addition reflects growing investment by Malaysian maritime companies in specialised assets and capabilities.
Lianson managing director Lim Chern Wooi said work was already lined up for the vessel ahead of its deployment and start of operations.
He said LFG Hercules will broaden the group's service offerings and provide opportunities in offshore decommissioning, heavy-lift work and offshore renewable energy infrastructure.
The acquisition marks Lianson's move into a larger and more specialised segment of the offshore support vessel and marine transportation market.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KPJ tops Asean healthcare brand strength, 2nd in value at US$305mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: KPJ Healthcare Bhd has emerged as Asean's strongest healthcare facilities brand, according to the Brand Finance Asean 500 2026 report, with a Brand Strength Index score of 86.8 out of 100.
The healthcare group also ranked second among Asean's most valuable healthcare facilities brands, after its brand value rose 45 per cent to US$305 million from US$211 million in 2025.
The increase followed a 71 per cent rise in brand value recorded a year earlier, marking a second consecutive year of growth.
KPJ climbed 49 places in the overall Asean 500 ranking to 182nd in 2026 from 231st previously, placing it among the region's 200 most valuable brands.
Officer-in-charge Prof Datuk Dr Hanafiah Harunarashid said the ranking reflects the confidence in the group.
KPJ is expanding its healthcare network through its KPJ Health System, which combines clinical practice, education, and research and innovation.
The group is also developing Centres of Excellence in areas including heart and lung care, neuroscience and stroke, and orthopaedics and rheumatology, with a target of 15 centres by 2030.
Its hospitals have also reported several recent clinical milestones, including robotic-assisted cardiac procedures and minimally invasive treatments.
KPJ plans to launch its Future Health Institute in 2027 to assess the application of research and digital health in clinical care.
Meanwhile, revenue from its health tourism segment rose 21 per cent year-on-year in the first half of 2026, supporting the group's regional healthcare business.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Data centre operators must bear electricity, infrastructure costs, says Johari
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: New data centre applications must take into account electricity supply availability and the ability of states to meet water demand, says Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
The investment, trade and industry minister said the growth of data centres must also be managed responsibly, with operators bearing the cost of electricity supply and necessary infrastructure.
"The cost of electricity supply and the necessary infrastructure must be borne by operators rather than passed on to the public or existing businesses.
"Our priority is to build a competitive digital economy while creating opportunities for local companies in power generation, energy storage and engineering.
"These investments must deliver tangible economic benefits through the efficient and sustainable use of national resources," he said in a Facebook post today.
Johari said he had delivered the keynote address at the Bursa Malaysia Sectoral Series: Powering the AI Era today.
He said Malaysia needed to be selective in attracting data centre investments, prioritising quality investments that generated added value for the economy while supporting the development of artificial intelligence (AI) and local industries.

Title: AmBank offers six-month flood relief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: AmBank Group is offering repayment assistance of up to six months to individual and small and medium enterprise customers affected by floods in parts of Selangor, including Shah Alam and Klang.
The assistance is also available to customers in other areas designated as flood disaster zones by the National Disaster Management Agency.
Under its flood relief programme, eligible customers may apply for a moratorium of up to six months on monthly financing payments.
The bank is also waiving incidental and replacement charges for cheque books, ATM and debit cards, and credit cards.
AmBank Group chief executive officer Jamie Ling said the assistance was intended to ease the financial burden on affected customers as they focus on recovery.
"We are ready to assist our customers as best as we can during this difficult period.
"Our relief assistance is aimed at alleviating the financial burden of our customers, so that they can focus on recovery and restoring their livelihoods," she said.
Affected customers can apply for the assistance and get more details through AmBank's flood relief programme.
Meanwhile, the bank advised customers to use its AmOnline mobile application and website for their banking needs.
Customers requiring further assistance may contact the AmBank Contact Centre, which operates from 9am to 9pm.

Title: 'Burning': Life under the world's dirtiest skies
Article:
ON the outskirts of India's capital, a short motorbike ride through the urban area with the world's worst air pollution leaves salesman Kanwar Singh coated in toxic dust.
"It enters my throat and lungs," the 55-year-old cigarette seller told AFP, running his hands over his clothes to show the fine dust.
"In the evening, I drink hot water and gargle... only then can I breathe easily."
But the dust he brushes off is not the most dangerous threat.
The toxic mix of traffic fumes, power station emissions and agricultural fires includes PM2.5 – fine particles that penetrate deep into the lungs, with some entering the bloodstream.
Long-term exposure increases the risk of lung cancer and heart disease.
Loni, where Singh lives, was one of five areas in the Delhi metropolitan region – home to around 30 million people – to feature among the world's 20 most polluted in an annual ranking by Swiss monitoring firm IQAir.
Four other Indian urban areas featured.
Over the year, Loni recorded average PM2.5 concentrations of 112.5 micrograms per cubic metre – more than 22 times the World Health Organisation (WHO)'s recommended annual limit of five micrograms.
During winter pollution peaks, when colder air traps pollutants close to the ground, PM2.5 readings can exceed 800 micrograms per cubic metre – more than 50 times the WHO's 24-hour guideline.
[[nid:1574804]]
Fireworks launched to celebrate the Hindu festival of Diwali also worsens the winter smog, with toxic air in parts of New Delhi soaring to more than 58 times the WHO's recommended daily limit on Monday.
Few residents wear masks, despite the choking dust. Many, like Singh, simply cover their faces with scarves or handkerchiefs.
"We are poor people," said Singh, who earns around US$5 a day. "If we had money, we would have bought a flat elsewhere."
Few can afford homes sealed against pollution or expensive air purifiers.
Loni, with a population of more than 700,000, according to latest census figures, is a densely packed industrial hub with factories involved in e-waste processing, textile dyeing, plastic recycling and metalworking.
Inspections by government air-quality officials in August found "widespread non-compliances" with environmental rules, including factories operating furnaces fuelled by wood and coal.
Poor roads, construction dust, vehicle emissions and the burning of dirty fuels compound the problem.
"My eyes are always burning here. I have trouble in my throat, a burning sensation in my eyes and people here fall sick very often, very quickly," housewife Savita Devi, 51, told AFP.
Mornings, when pollution hangs over the area before sunlight disperses some of the haze, also take a toll on her mental well-being.
"I just don't feel like doing anything," she said. "I makes me very uneasy."
The WHO lists air pollution as "one of the greatest environmental risks to child health."
[[nid:1574803]]
Air pollution was linked to an estimated 17,188 deaths in Delhi in 2023, nearly 15 percent of the total, making it the city's biggest individual risk factor, an analysis by Finland-based Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA) found.
Devi said her grandchildren often fell sick when pollution levels surged.
"If you consult a doctor, he will say it's infection," she said. "But here, infections happen because of this pollution."
Authorities have deployed water-sprinkler trucks to suppress road dust, but the measure does little to tackle finer PM2.5 pollution from traffic and industry.
"A dust-free road is everyone's responsibility," a roadside government hoarding reads.
The relief is fleeting, residents said, with dust returning within an hour as traffic and construction churn it back into the air.
"Dust keeps coming," said shopkeeper Inamul Khan, 27. "We have to wash things two or three times, all our clothes, bedding, everything gets ruined," he added.
He watched as a sprinkler truck sprayed an adjoining road under construction.
"When there's so many crowds and road construction going on, how much can they do?"
For Singh, who has respiratory problems, the worst days mean staying indoors, but also means he cannot earn.
"I keep a face mask or cloth on, and take my medicine just to stay alive," he said.
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: ‘Alhamdulillah’: Rosmah welcomes news of Najib’s clearance for house arrest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor has expressed gratitude following the return of her husband, former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, to their residence in Jalan Langgak Duta here today after a court order allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house detention.
“Alhamdulillah,” Rosmah said briefly when contacted by
Berita Harian
.
She said she was awaiting Najib’s arrival at their Taman Duta home, where he will serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house detention.
Earlier today, the High Court issued a fresh order allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his reduced six-year prison term under house detention until Aug 23, 2028, with immediate effect.
A survey of the area found the atmosphere outside the residence calm, with security arrangements in place as preparations were made for Najib’s return home.
Najib’s house detention follows recent legal developments concerning the implementation of the remainder of his sentence.

Title: Investigation papers on Penang assemblyman accused of injuring wife still under DPP review
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 10 — Penang police are awaiting further instructions from the Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) on the investigation into an allegation that a state assemblyman injured his wife in an incident on October 31.
Penang Chief Police Officer Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the investigation papers were still with the DPP's office for further review.
"The investigation papers are still with the DPP, and police are awaiting further instructions on the case," he told Bernama when contacted tonight for an update on the investigation.
Earlier, police confirmed receiving a report from the assemblyman's wife, who alleged that her husband had injured her at their home here on Oct 31.
Lim was previously reported as saying that police had opened an investigation paper under Section 323 of the Penal Code to investigate the incident. — Bernama

Title: Home Ministry says ready to carry out Najib’s house arrest; court order today cleared the air
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — The Home Ministry this evening said it is prepared to carry out a new court order today for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to be on house arrest until August 2028.
In his statement on his ministry’s readiness to execute the court’s new order, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the High Court’s latest order has helped answered legal uncertainties surrounding Najib’s house arrest.
He was referring to the High Court in Kuala Lumpur’s decision this afternoon to revoke an earlier November 6 “Order of Discharge on Payment of Fine” and to replace it with a new order that will require Najib to serve his remaining jail term under house arrest until August 23, 2028.
The house arrest will be at Najib’s private residence at No 11, Jalan Langgak Duta, Taman Duta in Kuala Lumpur.
Najib, who was wearing a light blue
baju Melayu
top, was brought from Kajang Prison and was present at the court proceedings this afternoon.
On November 6, Umno had paid the RM50 million fine on behalf of Najib, as this was the condition in the Yang di-Pertuan Agong’s September conditional pardon to allow him to be on house arrest in the SRC International case.
But Najib had remained in Kajang Prison since November 6, as the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) had highlighted legal uncertainties related to Najib’s house arrest.
Earlier today, the AGC filed an application at the High Court to rectify or correct the earlier court order and also to issue a new court order that would enable the house arrest, which resulted in this afternoon’s court proceedings.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail explained that the delay in implementing Najib’s house arrest previously was due to legal issues regarding interpretation of the conditional pardon order and the legal effect of the November 6 “Order of Discharge”, especially regarding the implementation of the remaining sentence via house arrest. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
Saifuddin today said the Home Ministry always respects and upholds the Agong’s royal pardon decision in line with the ruler’s powers under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution, and that all decisions made through constitutional channels should be respected and carried out according to the law.
Saifuddin then explained that the delay in implementing Najib’s house arrest previously was due to legal issues regarding interpretation of the conditional pardon order and the legal effect of the November 6 “Order of Discharge”, especially regarding the implementation of the remaining sentence via house arrest.
“The High Court’s decision today has clarified this issue,” he said in his statement that was titled as the government’s position on the implementation of the royal pardon involving Najib.
He said the Home Ministry respects the AGC’s position that the legal issue required clarification through a court process, adding that this approach is important to ensure each government action has a clear and valid legal basis.
“As Home Minister, I stress that the Ministry’s and the Prisons Department’s responsibility is to ensure that each decision related to the execution of sentence and detention is carried out according to the law and valid court orders,” he said in his statement.
“This case is a high-profile case which has huge political implications and public perception,” he said, urging for everyone to handle this maturely and responsibly without letting political polemics from affecting public confidence in the country’s institution.
Saifuddin concluded by saying that the federal government would continue to defend the Malay rulers’ role and position within the framework of Malaysia’s constitutional monarchy, while upholding constitutional supremacy, rule of law and the judiciary’s independence.
“These principles complete each other and are the basis for national stability,” he concluded.
While Najib will be able to serve the rest of his SRC International jail term at home until August 23, 2028, he is also facing a separate 15-year jail term in his other trial involving over RM2 billion of 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) funds.
The High Court in December 2025 had ordered Najib to immediately start serving his 15-year jail term in the 1MDB case after he completes his SRC International jail term.
Najib is currently appealing his 1MDB conviction and jail term, with the Court of Appeal yet to hear his appeal.

Title: How uncertainty over university pathways shapes Chinese youths’ choices
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — For some Malaysian Chinese youths, deciding where to study after secondary school is not simply a matter of choosing a course or university.
Most of these choices are made through weighing how secure they feel about their chances of getting into their preferred programme.
In a research conducted by IMAN Research, they found that uncertainty over public university admissions, differences between pre-university pathways and concerns about access to certain courses had influenced how some the research participants approached their education.
In its recently published report,
Kami Orang Sini Juga: Chinese Youths and Democratic Belonging — The Politics of Pragmatism and Fairness
, draws on interviews with 116 Malaysian Chinese youths aged between 18 and 35 across Peninsular Malaysia.
The study found that education was one of the areas where participants’ perceptions of fairness were particularly shaped by their own experiences, expectations and accounts they had heard from others.
Some participants described choosing private education or overseas study rather than applying through the public university admission system.
One interviewee, for instance, went directly to a private university without applying through the Unit Pusat Universiti (UPU), citing concerns within the family about the chances of securing a place through the public route.
Another participant who wanted to study medicine declined an offer to pursue biotechnology and instead went to China.
The report describes these decisions as examples of how young people may seek alternatives when public pathways appear uncertain.
However, it also makes an important distinction between barriers participants personally experienced, obstacles they anticipated and accounts they had heard from family members or their wider community.
These are not the same kinds of evidence, and the researchers cautioned against treating every disappointing outcome or decision not to apply as proof of discrimination.
Matriculation and UPU are not the same
The research found that there was a recurring source of confusion among participants — the relationship between the matriculation quota and university admissions through UPU.
The report clarifies that the 90 per cent Bumiputera quota applies to entry into matriculation, not to UPU’s university selection formula.
UPU ranks applicants from STPM, matriculation and other equivalent qualifications using 90 per cent academic marks and 10 per cent co-curricular marks.
Candidates are considered according to merit, programme requirements, available places and their course preferences.
The report said the UPU pathway itself does not have an ethnic quota system.
However, the researchers noted that differences between Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM) and matriculation could still raise questions about fairness.
STPM generally takes one and a half years, while the main matriculation programme takes one year.
The two pathways also use different assessment structures.
How are they different?
STPM students may progress through school, zone, district, state and national competitions, while matriculation students compete within a structure centred on inter-college competitions.
Citing figures that showed 16 per cent of matriculation students achieved a cumulative grade point average of 4.0, compared with 3.09 per cent of STPM students, the researchers suggest these differences be examined when considering how students from the two pathways are assessed
For popular courses such as medicine, pharmacy and dentistry at public universities, matriculation students accounted for more than 97 per cent of places in 2023, while STPM students made up less than 3 per cent, according to figures cited in the report.
These figures were used to illustrate differences in outcomes between the pathways, rather than establish that any individual applicant had been unfairly treated.
When students look for alternatives
The report found that family resources played an important role in determining whether young people could pursue alternatives when they felt uncertain about public education pathways.
Some could afford private universities or overseas study, while others had fewer options.
This meant that the ability to work around perceived barriers was not equally available to everyone.
The researchers also noted that concerns inherited from parents or community members could influence decisions even before a student applied for a place.
In such cases, these Chinese youths people might rule out a pathway based on what they had heard about the system, rather than on a direct experience of rejection.
The report recommends that the government make university admissions criteria, selection mechanisms and intake data more transparent and accessible.
It also calls for students to be given clearer information about how different pre-university qualifications are assessed and how they affect university options.
The researchers said differences in co-curricular opportunities between STPM and matriculation should also be reviewed, alongside clearer pathways for students holding the Unified Examination Certificate who wish to enter public universities.
Rather than redesigning the entire pre-university system, the report suggests addressing specific areas where the students face uncertainty or unequal opportunities.
Its broader concern is that when students cannot clearly understand how public education pathways work, they may make decisions based on assumptions, family experiences or perceived limitations — potentially narrowing their choices before they have fully explored them.

Title: Najib’s house arrest: What did the AGC ask the High Court to clarify today?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) today sought to ensure that Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest arrangements explicitly provided for his return to Kajang Prison on August 24, 2028, to serve his separate 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) prison sentence.
In its written application, the prosecution requested that the High Court replace a November 6 discharge order with new terms clarifying Najib’s remaining SRC International sentence and his subsequent imprisonment in the 1MDB case.
The application specified that Najib should “be transferred back to Kajang Prison on August 24, 2028, to serve the sentence imposed on him in the 1MDB case”.
It also sought to specify that his SRC sentence would end on August 23, 2028, with his return to prison subject to any court order then in force.
The prosecution said the 1MDB prison sentence had been directed to begin once his SRC sentence ended, arguing that “the end date of the SRC sentences must be stated with certainty”.
It explained that Najib’s payment of the RM50 million fine on November 6 discharged his liability for the fine and imprisonment for non-payment, but did not extinguish his remaining SRC prison sentence.
The AGC also argued that the earlier discharge order, which used a standard form for release upon payment of a fine, could be interpreted as releasing Najib from his remaining SRC sentence altogether.
Citing provisions of the Criminal Procedure Code governing imprisonment warrants, the prosecution said there was an urgent need for a clear order in accordance with the law.
High Court grants AGC’s application
High Court judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin subsequently granted the prosecution’s application, setting aside the November 6 discharge order and allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his SRC sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028.
According to Bernama, Judge Aslam said the court would replace the earlier order “entirely with the order sought in this application”.
The new order also provides for Najib’s return to Kajang Prison on August 24, 2028, to serve his separate 1MDB sentence, Bernama reported.
At the hearing, Najib’s lead counsel Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah had argued that the original discharge order was already clear, as the RM50 million fine required under the conditional royal pardon had been paid.
Speaking to reporters afterwards, Shafee welcomed the court’s clarification despite maintaining that the original order was sound.

Title: Rapid KL confirms brake fault behind smoke incident at KL Sentral (VIDEO)
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Rapid KL today confirmed an incident involving one of its trains at KL Sentral station after smoke was seen coming from the train at about 5.15pm.
In a statement, the rail operator said the incident is believed to have been caused by the train's braking system, which resulted in visible smoke being emitted from the affected train.
As a safety precaution, the train was immediately withdrawn from service and will undergo a detailed inspection at the depot.
Rapid KL said all passengers were safely disembarked at Bangsar station and were able to continue their journey on the next available train.
No injuries were reported in the incident.
The operator added that train services on the Kelana Jaya Line continue to operate as normal despite the disruption.
Rapid KL also apologised to affected passengers for the inconvenience caused and reiterated that passenger safety remains its top priority.
