Title: Beyond assumptions: IMAN Research’s journey into the lives of Chinese youths
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — When Violet Lee Zi Yi began researching Malaysian Chinese youths, she admitted she initially approached the community with assumptions about its relative economic advantages, resources and access to opportunities.
What she discovered through interviews with these youths across Peninsular Malaysia was a much more complicated picture.
“I initially thought Chinese is a unitary block. It is so different,” Lee said in an interview about the findings of IMAN Research’s report,
Kami Orang Sini Juga: Chinese Youths and Democratic Belonging — The Politics of Pragmatism and Fairness
.
The report, prepared by Lee and co-researcher Liew Liang Hong, is based on interviews with 116 Malaysian Chinese youths aged between 18 and 35 conducted from August 2025 to April 2026.
It examines Chinese youths on how they understand their identity, navigate opportunities and inequality, and relate to politics and public institutions.
Rather than treating Malaysian Chinese youths as a single political or cultural group, the research found that their experiences were shaped by factors including family history, language, schooling, religion, socioeconomic background and where they grew up.
For some, regional identities such as being Penangite, Johorean or an anak Terengganu were just as important in defining who they were.
“When I started the research, I went into it with a mindset of —
apa lagi Cina mahu
or what else do the Chinese want?
“I wanted to understand what more Malaysian Chinese youths wanted, so I had assumptions about the community’s relative advantages.
“But the interviews changed my perception. Everyone’s experience is so diverse, so different, and every conversation just added what I had never imagined before,” she said.
One example was how family history could shape identity differently across generations.
Lee said she had not initially considered how being a third-generation Malaysian Chinese could produce a different outlook from being fourth-generation, depending on how grandparents and great-grandparents had spoken about China and their family’s history.
She said these differences emerged naturally during the conversations, illustrating how the research uncovered experiences that the team had not anticipated when designing its questions.
Belonging is not always straightforward
The report found that national identity did not necessarily come at the expense of Chinese cultural identity.
Some participants described themselves primarily as Malaysian, while others considered Malaysian Chinese an inseparable identity.
Others placed strong emphasis on their state or hometown.
For some interviewees from the East Coast, being an anak Terengganu was central to how they described home, even as they recognised restrictions associated with being part of a minority community.
One participant described the distinction between feeling at home and feeling politically restricted, saying: “As a layman I feel I belong, but in politics I feel being restricted, like in Matriculation and fund allocation.”
The report said these feelings could coexist: participants could feel emotionally attached to Malaysia while questioning how public resources and institutions treated different communities.
It also found that everyday interactions could foster a sense of shared Malaysian identity.
Participants spoke positively about ordinary experiences such as eating at mamak restaurants, mixing languages and joining one another’s festivals.
However, the researchers cautioned against romanticising these interactions, noting that cordial relationships did not necessarily translate into deeper understanding or erase concerns about institutional fairness.
The cost of pragmatism
One of the report’s central findings is what it calls “self-cornering” — the tendency to find private ways around perceived problems rather than challenge the institutions behind them.
The report found that some young people responded to uncertainty over public opportunities by working harder, relying on family networks, paying for alternatives or looking overseas.
These decisions could be practical and help individuals secure their futures, but the researchers argued that they also carried wider consequences.
When those with sufficient resources could find private alternatives, the institutions and policies behind their concerns remained unchanged. Those without the means to find alternatives could be left with fewer options.
The report also distinguished between inequality personally experienced by participants, barriers they anticipated and accounts they had heard from family or community members.
It cautioned against treating every disappointing outcome as proof of discrimination, while recognising that inherited accounts could influence how young people assessed their prospects.
Wanting to be heard
Another finding concerned the distance between young people and the organisations or institutions expected to represent them.
Lee said she was struck by how some interviewees did not consider their own opinions valuable simply because they were not politically vocal.
“We wanted to include young people who were not already active in community organisations or political circles, rather than relying mainly on those who were accustomed to speaking publicly.
“Only about 10 to 15 per cent of those recruited were young leaders.
“This was important because young people who were already involved in organisations were often more comfortable expressing their views, while others might not see their own experiences as worth sharing,” she said.
The research team also found that established community leaders could say they wanted younger people to participate, yet were sometimes reluctant to give them meaningful space.
Lee said this could leave young people struggling to find where they could contribute, while older leaders continued to hold the resources and decision-making positions.
She also questioned the narrow definition of success within parts of the community, where financial achievement and professional status could be valued more visibly than civic or political participation.
“Chinese youth are not rewarded socially if you are in politics. Only if you become a politician, you become someone famous, then yes, you’re recognised,” she said.
Those working behind the scenes, she added, were less likely to receive recognition.
Lee said the research also found that some young people wanted to move beyond racialised political thinking but were unsure how to do so.
“They are conditioned in the racial politics. They are conditioned into thinking along the communal lines, but they want to break through that.”
Among the many challenges
She said one challenge for the researchers was to ensure that the findings did not simply reflect the views of the loudest or most visible members of the community.
“Being the loudest did not mean that they have a full understanding of a stipulation on ground,” she said.
Not particularly looking for a solution, Lee said the report is a qualitative research and is not statistically representative of all Malaysian Chinese youths.
“Its findings are intended to provide insight into how the participants understood their experiences, rather than measure how widespread particular views are.
“We actually only included 30 per cent of the data collected, there were just too much data which we thought was better to leave them for further research into specific communities and experiences,” she said.
For Lee, the next step is to create more opportunities for young people from different communities to speak to one another.
She said the responsibility should not fall on young people alone, but also on researchers, the media and civil society organisations to create space for discussion.
For her, the research is ultimately about giving young people more room to think about their place in the country, rather than seeing them only as voters whose views matter during elections.
“This research gets the conversation starting especially for Chinese youths who don’t know where to start, or what to do first,” she said.

Title: Anthony Loke officially resigns as transport minister following court decision on Najib
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook has resigned as transport minister with immediate effect following the Kuala Lumpur High Court's decision allowing former prime minister Najib Tun Razak to serve his sentence under house arrest, according to a statement issued today.
In the statement, Loke said his decision was in line with the position he had publicly stated last Friday and was based on the principles and stand he had previously outlined.
He expressed his appreciation to Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim for the trust and mandate given to him to serve in the Cabinet since December 2022.
Loke also thanked the senior management and staff of the Ministry of Transport for their commitment and cooperation throughout his tenure at the ministry. He said he would provide full cooperation to ensure a smooth transition and that all ministry responsibilities and initiatives would continue to be implemented in the interest of the public.

Title: Najib to serve remaining jail term at home after High Court issues new warrant
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — The High Court has directed the Court Registrar to issue a new order that would finally allow Datuk Seri Mohd Najib Abdul Razak to serve the remaining sentence of his first corruption conviction at home.
High Court Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin issued the new warrant of release after hearing submissions by both Najib’s lawyers and the Deputy Public Prosecutors this afternoon.
Judge Aslam said the new order simply cancels the November 6 order and replaced with one that allows Najib to serve the remaining sentence from the said conviction at home.
“I will just read the gist of it: The order dated November 6 is hereby cancelled and is a replaced with a new order that states the defendant will serve his remaining sentence under house imprisonment,” he said.
At the hearing, Najib’s lead counsel Tan Sri Shafee Abdullah had argued that the court need not issue a new order since the first was already “very clear”.
He alleged even the Prison Department understood the discharge order, was ready to release the former prime minister but “was then told to wait”.
Shafee’s core argument was that the condition to trigger Najib’s release from Kajang Prison and serve home imprisonment - paying the RM50 million - was already met, and that the ensuing order of discharge issued by the High Court Registrar was worded in a way that reflected that.
In a press conference held shortly after the hearing ended, Shafee welcomed the clarification by Judge Aslam even has he maintained his argument that the original order was “solid in substance”, and that all matters regarding the King’s pardon need not be formalised by the judicial system.
“It is good that the court has clarified so that those who apparently found it hard to understand, will now understand,” he said.
Najib, in a light blue baju melayu top with sleeves rolled up, was present at the hearing alongside his daughter Najwa, who was also in a blue floral baju kurung.
The former prime minister was set to serve the remaining two years of his jail sentence from the corruption conviction involving SRC International arrest last Friday, after his lawyers said he had paid the RM50 million fine as part of his conditional pardon.
The AGC, however, delayed his release from Kajang Prison, claiming it needed clarification because the November 6 court order was unclear and possibly defective.
Shafee said Najib would likely be home by tonight, after all formal documents have been submitted to Kajang Prison where he would also be briefed about the conditions of his house arrest.
Details of the conditions are still not available to the lawyers for now including on visitation Shafee added.
“I assume you will have to apply, at least initially. Or they may make it easier as there is a post (at Najib’s residence), and they may device some system,” he said.
“But nevertheless, the point being you will still need to get permission.”
It is understood that Najib’s house arrest will last until August 2028.

Title: ITU PP-26: Appointment of Malaysian representative as Committee 5 chair reflects international confidence
Article:
DOHA, Nov 10 — Malaysia’s appointment as chair of Committee 5 at the 2026 International Telecommunication Union Plenipotentiary Conference (ITU PP-26) reflects the international community’s confidence in the country’s ability to play a neutral role in balancing the interests of various parties.
Committee 5 chair Eneng Faridah Iskandar said the appointment was not merely a personal recognition but a major achievement for Malaysia, according to a report published by Bernama.
“I think this is not only an achievement (but) actually an achievement for the country because Malaysia is seen as a neutral country that can accept the views of all parties.
“So, as chair, our task is to balance the interests and wishes of all parties, and we must be fair,” she told Bernama and RTM here today.
Eneng Faridah, who is also Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) Deputy Managing Director (Development), expressed her appreciation to the Malaysian government for having the confidence to nominate her for the role at the conference, which runs from November 9 to 27.
She said the position carried significant responsibility as she would not only represent Malaysia but also have to take into account the interests of all member states involved in the discussions.
Explaining Committee 5’s role, Eneng Faridah said the substantive committee was responsible for examining various policy and legal issues within the ITU framework.
More than 95 proposals covering over 40 resolutions have been submitted for discussion at this year’s conference.
“One of the main challenges is acting as an intermediary between various parties with different interests to reach a common agreement, as the ITU operates on the principle of consensus,” she said.
She said several preliminary meetings had been held ahead of the committee’s sessions, which are scheduled to begin tomorrow, to ensure that negotiations proceed smoothly.
One of the main committees at ITU PP-26, Committee 5, also known as the Policy and Legal Committee, is responsible for discussing proposed international telecommunications policies and regulations, as well as examining resolutions submitted by ITU member states.
Its chair plays a key role in conducting negotiations, balancing interests and bridging differences among member states to reach a consensus, before the committee’s deliberations are submitted to the conference for consideration and decisions.
PP-26, being held in Doha, is the ITU’s highest-level conference, convened every four years to determine the organisation’s direction, policies and strategic plans.
The Malaysian delegation to the conference is led by Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, with the mission of retaining the country’s seat on the ITU Council for the 2027-2030 term.
The ITU is a specialised agency of the United Nations (UN) responsible for information and communications technology (ICT), including setting global standards, allocating radio-frequency spectrum, coordinating satellites and efforts to bridge the global digital divide.

Title: MWC Doha: Fahmi shares Malaysia’s 5G network progress, 90pc coverage achieved ahead of schedule
Article:
DOHA, Nov 10 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil shared Malaysia’s progress in expanding its 5G network at Mobile World Congress (MWC) Doha 2026, with the country’s second 5G network achieving 90 per cent coverage last October, nine months ahead of schedule.
He said the achievement marked significant progress in Malaysia’s transition towards a dual 5G network model aimed at enhancing competition, encouraging investment and improving the quality of telecommunications services, according to a Bernama report.
Fahmi said Malaysia had also made substantial investments in expanding and strengthening its digital infrastructure through the National Digital Network Plan (Jendela) since 2020.
“As of July 2026, approximately 10.12 million premises had been covered by fibre-optic networks, significantly improving access to high-speed broadband services,” he said during the Ministerial Panel Forum on Digital Leadership at MWC Doha 2026 here on Sunday.
He said the developments reflected the country’s efforts to build a competitive and sustainable telecommunications ecosystem while ensuring consumers benefited from improved service quality.
However, Fahmi stressed that Malaysia’s digital infrastructure development was not solely focused on expanding network coverage, but also on service quality, subscription affordability and network resilience.
He said all these aspects needed to be addressed comprehensively to ensure digital connectivity delivered meaningful benefits to the people.
“Through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), we continue to encourage infrastructure sharing and efficient network deployment, while addressing connectivity gaps among underserved communities,” he said.
Fahmi said the Universal Service Provision (USP) framework also played an important role in extending telecommunications services to areas that might not be commercially viable through private investment alone.
He said this approach allowed Malaysia to balance infrastructure investment with the need to ensure telecommunications services remained accessible at affordable rates.
“For Malaysia, a successful network model is one that combines strong infrastructure, sustainable investment, effective regulation and meaningful access for all,” he said.
Fahmi is in Doha to lead the Malaysian delegation to the International Telecommunication Union Plenipotentiary Conference (ITU PP-26), which runs from November 6 to 11.
His working visit also carries the important mission of securing Malaysia’s re-election to the ITU Council for the 2027-2030 term.
He is accompanied by Communications Ministry Deputy Secretary-General (Telecommunications Infrastructure) Mano Verabathran.
The Malaysian delegation also includes representatives from the MCMC and local telecommunications industry players, including Telekom Malaysia (TM), CelcomDigi, Maxis and U Mobile.

Title: Kuala Kangsar Sessions Court orders mental health assessment for accused in rape, attempted murder case
Article:
KUALA KANGSAR, Nov 10 — The Sessions Court here today ordered a man who pleaded guilty to attempting to murder and raping a woman to undergo a psychiatric assessment at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta, Tanjung Rambutan.
Judge Nuur Hafiedzah Md Daud issued the order against Marwan Mohd Nor, 38, under Section 342 of the Criminal Procedure Code after observing the accused’s demeanour when he pleaded guilty to both charges.
Earlier, Marwan pleaded guilty to both charges and appealed to the court to impose the maximum sentence for the rape charge.
According to the first charge, the accused was alleged to have attempted to murder a 20-year-old woman, causing her injuries by the roadside along the Felda Lasah-Lintang road, at Lubuk Kelah Lintang, Sungai Siput, at about 11.20 pm on Nov 3.
The charge was framed under Section 307(1) of the Penal Code, which provides for a jail term of up to 20 years and a possible fine upon conviction.
Under the second charge, the man was accused of causing injury to and raping the victim at the same location, date and time.
He was charged under Section 376(2)(a) of the Penal Code, which provides for a minimum jail term of 10 years and a maximum of 30 years, as well as whipping, upon conviction.
Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) prosecuting officer Insp Nor A’in Ahmad applied for a date to be fixed for the submission of the facts of the case and sentencing.
The court subsequently ordered the accused to be sent to Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta Tanjung Rambutan for monitoring and a mental health assessment, and fixed Dec 21 for mention of the case and submission of the psychiatric report. — Bernama

Title: Not cutting-edge: Men armed with scissors in Tuaran gang robbery to be sentenced on Nov 20
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 10 — Three men who pleaded guilty to a charge of gang robbery armed with scissors will know their fate on November 20.
Sessions Court Judge Monica Linsua adjourned the sentencing of the men, aged 29, 26, and 35 respectively, under Section 395 of the Penal Code, which is punishable under Section 397 of the same Code, at the request of the prosecution.
The prosecution had requested ample time to prepare the facts of the case and relevant documents before the court passed the sentence.
The men had admitted robbing another two men of their cash and two mobile phones by the roadside of Jalan Berungis in Tuaran at 12.50am on Oct 26.
The charge stated that the offence was committed with another two accomplices, who are still at large.
The offence carries a jail term of up to 20 years and caning upon conviction.
The three men were released on RM5,000 bail each with one local surety.
Monica also ordered them to report to the nearest police station once a month until the disposal of the case.
Deputy public prosecutor Fazriel Fardiansyah Abdul Kadir appeared for the prosecution, while all three men did not have legal counsel. — The Borneo Post

Title: Najib in court as lawyers, AGC discuss fresh house arrest order
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Datuk Seri Najib Razak is present as the High Court hears the application for a new order to allow the former prime minister to serve his first jail sentence at home.
Najib, in a light blue baju melayu top with sleeves rolled up, was present at the hearing alongside his daughter Najwa, who was in a blue floral baju kurung.
The former prime minister was set to serve the remaining two years of his jail sentence from the corruption conviction involving SRC International last Friday, after his lawyers said he had paid the RM50 million fine as part of his conditional pardon.
The AGC, however, delayed his release from Kajang Prison, claiming it needed clarification because the November 6 court order was unclear and possibly defective.
The High Court is expected to issue a new warrant to release Najib from Kajang Prison this afternoon itself.

Title: Melaka polls: Pakatan takes politics to coffee shops with Gen Z-focused ‘Kopilih Harapan’ initiative
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 10 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is adopting a new approach to engage young people, particularly Generation Z, through its ‘Kopilih Harapan’ programme, which provides an informal platform for political leaders and members of the public to discuss current issues and aspirations.
PH Election Department (JPPH) Media Unit head Jonathan Vela said the programme aims to foster more open and inclusive two-way communication, moving away from conventional political ceramah.
He said the coffee shop-themed initiative allows young people to raise questions, share their views and seek clarification directly from PH leaders and candidates.
“We want to provide them with a platform to discuss and exchange views, rather than simply listen to political speeches. It also gives them an opportunity to get to know their leaders and understand politics better,” he told a press conference at the PH Main Operations Room in Bukit Piatu here today.
Jonathan said the programme would feature Lembah Jaya assemblyman Syed Ahmad Syed Abdul Rahman Al-Hadad, better known as Altimet, Bentong Member of Parliament Young Syefura Othman, Hang Tuah Jaya MP Adam Adli Abd Halim and several other PH leaders.
He said Kopilih Harapan would visit several locations frequented by young people across the state during the 16th Melaka state election campaign, in collaboration with local coffee shops, while also supporting small-scale entrepreneurs and the local coffee industry.
Meanwhile, Altimet, who is also the Kopilih Harapan ambassador, said the initiative took into account changing media consumption habits among younger generations, who were increasingly accustomed to interactive communication rather than one-way information delivery.
“Based on my experience, engaging with them through a forum that is not in the form of a political speech but rather a dialogue session is more effective.
“We also give them the opportunity to decide what they want to discuss. When we share the direction of the session with them, young people feel that they are part of the programme,” said the former rapper.
Altimet said the approach should be expanded beyond PH, including among Members of Parliament and state assemblymen, to engage the public, particularly young voters.
Polling is set for Nov 14. For the latest updates on the 16th Melaka state election, visit
https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/
. — Bernama

Title: Skilled workforce crucial to unlocking Malaysia’s high-tech investment potential, says minister
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Nov 10 — Developing a highly skilled workforce must remain a priority for Malaysia to fully capitalise on opportunities arising from digital transformation and the rapid growth of high-tech industries.
Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Chang Lih Kang said that while Malaysia continues to attract billions of ringgit in high-tech sector investments, the country’s success ultimately depends on its local workforce’s ability to master and harness emerging technologies.
“Malaysia is currently at the forefront of the regional digital transformation, with global companies choosing the country as an investment destination for artificial intelligence (AI), semiconductor manufacturing, smart factories and renewable energy, further strengthening our position as the digital backbone of the Asia-Pacific region.
“However, behind these investments lies a fundamental truth: machines do not build nations, people do,” he said at the official opening of Schneider Electric’s Regional Training Center (RTC) here today.
Chang said the rapid adoption of digitalisation, advanced automation and complex electrification had increased demand for workers with technical expertise and skills aligned with industry requirements.
“Without equipping our engineers, technicians and young Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) talents with practical, industry-relevant skills, we risk leaving our workforce behind as technology continues to advance,” he added.
He said initiatives such as Schneider Electric’s RTC were important in bridging the gap between academic education and industry requirements while preparing Malaysians for opportunities in the growing digital economy.
Chang said industry investments in human capital development also reinforced the principle that Malaysia’s greatest asset was its people, ensuring national innovation policies translated into tangible economic outcomes.
He also highlighted Malaysia’s achievement in securing 34th place out of 139 economies in the 2026 Global Innovation Index.
Malaysia recorded more than RM200 billion in approved investments in the first half of this year, including RM95 billion in data centres and cloud infrastructure, particularly in Selangor and Johor.
The 18,500-square-foot facility can train more than 550 participants annually from 15 Asia-Pacific countries through hands-on technical exercises using operational equipment and real-world industry scenarios.
Chang officiated the opening ceremony. Also present were French Ambassador to Malaysia Marc Abensour, Malaysian French Chamber of Commerce and Industry president Richard Fostier and Schneider Electric Malaysia country president Eugene Quah.
The event also coincides with Schneider Electric’s 40th anniversary in Malaysia, marking four decades of the company’s contribution to the country’s industrial development, energy transition and technological advancement. — Bernama

Title: Police deployed outside Najib’s residence amid home detention rumours
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Police maintained a presence outside former prime minister Najib Razak's residence today as speculation grew over his possible return home under a reported house arrest arrangement.
According to
China Press,
several police vehicles and personnel were seen stationed near the property in Jalan Langgak Duta throughout the day. Media personnel and members of the public also gathered outside the residence following widespread rumours that Najib could be transferred from prison to serve the remainder of his sentence at home.
Authorities, however, did not provide immediate confirmation on any transfer, while legal and administrative procedures were understood to still be under consideration.
Najib, who is serving a prison sentence after being convicted in the SRC International case, has been at the centre of ongoing legal proceedings and discussions regarding a purported royal addendum order related to home detention.
As of late afternoon, no transfer had taken place and officials had yet to announce any final decision. Police remained on standby while awaiting further instructions from the relevant authorities.

Title: Pertak river water surge: Search for three missing victims widened to Sungai Selangor dam
Article:
HULU SELANGOR, Nov 10 — The search and rescue (SAR) operation for three people still missing following a water surge incident at Lata Jebus, near the Sungai Pertak waterfall in Kampung Pertak here, has been extended to the Sungai Selangor Dam, about three kilometres from the scene.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said search efforts were concentrated along Sungai Luit, from Lata Jebus towards the dam.
“The search area has been expanded to cover a stretch of about three kilometres along Sungai Luit, from the incident site to the Sungai Selangor Dam,” he told reporters at the scene.
Ashrul Riezal said the first victim, identified as V. Vijayan, 36, was found near the Pertak Bridge at 1.30am today, about 2.7 kilometres from where he was swept away.
Four other victims were found near the Senget Bridge and the suspension bridge at about 10.12 am today, about one kilometre from Lata Jebus, but their identities and nationalities have yet to be confirmed.
In the incident at about 5.30pm yesterday, eight people comprising a Yemeni, a Malaysian, a Sri Lankan, a Nepalese and four Indian nationals were swept away by strong currents.
A check at the scene found that a police truck carrying the bodies of four victims left the Incident Command Post (ICP) at about noon today.
It is learnt that the bodies were taken to Sungai Buloh Hospital for post-mortem examinations.
Meanwhile, Vijayan's relative, B. Partiban, 27, said he arrived at the waterfall after Vijayan, who had gone there with a group of foreign friends.
“The water suddenly surged at about 5.30pm, carrying logs and debris. It was flowing so fast that we could only stand there and watch,” he said.
Partiban said he and three friends managed to move to safety before the water level rose sharply, but were unaware that Vijayan had been swept away by the current.
Another survivor, Muhammad, 19, a Yemeni student, said there were no signs of danger when he and five friends arrived at the river, but a sudden surge of water swept away three of his friends near the riverbank, leaving one still missing.
In the latest development, Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director Datuk Wan Md Razali Wan Ismail said in a statement that authorities had confirmed the identities of two of the four victims found this morning.
He said they were identified as Kapali, 49, from Nepal, and B. Kunjunmaiayil, 35, from India.
Wan Md Razali said today’s search and rescue operation involved 45 JBPM personnel, 25 from the Civil Defence Force (APM), three police officers and five members of the Batang Kali Volunteer Fire Brigade.
The operation also involved three personnel each from the Hulu Selangor Land Office and Hulu Selangor Municipal Council (MPHS), along with two mountain guides. — Bernama

Title: Johor pawn shop heist: Seven arrested, former manager suspected of masterminding RM28.4m theft, says police chief
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 10 — A 44-year-old former female manager of a pawn shop in Kota Tinggi is believed to have masterminded a break-in at the premises that resulted in the loss of jewellery and cash totaling RM28.4 million last Friday.
Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the suspect allegedly entered the premises through the front entrance and exited through the back with the items and cash at 11.42am.
Acting on information, he said police arrested seven individuals, consisting of five men and two women.
“The suspects are all locals aged between 29 and 48.
“They were arrested separately in Kota Tinggi and Johor Bahru on November 7 and 8 to assist with the investigation,” he told reporters at the Johor police contingent headquarters here today.
Following the arrests, Ab Rahaman said police seized 2,891 pieces of jewellery, RM27,371 in cash, two pawn receipts, two sets of keys, two sling bags and a mobile phone.
He said that investigations suggest the motive behind the incident was to destroy evidence pertaining to a criminal breach of trust case committed by the former manager.
“Most of the jewellery taken were actually fake or costume jewellery, pawned by the suspect’s associates using the identities of non-existent individuals to fraudulently obtain the company’s funds,” he said.
Ab Rahaman said that background checks revealed one of the suspects has two prior criminal records, while initial urine screening tests for all suspects returned negative for drugs.
“Four suspects have been remanded for seven days, from November 8 to 14, while three others have been remanded until this Sunday to assist with the probe,” he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 457 of the Penal Code for theft and Section 408 of the Penal Code for criminal breach of trust.

Title: Vehicle believed to be carrying Najib seen leaving Kajang Prison amid court proceedings over house arrest order
Article:
KAJANG, Nov 10 — A grey sport utility vehicle (SUV) believed to be carrying former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak was seen leaving the Kajang Prison Complex at about 2.40pm today, escorted by several prison security vehicles.
The
New Straits Times
(NST) reported that the convoy comprised five vehicles, but its destination was not immediately known.
The departure came as Najib’s lawyers were scheduled to attend a court mention over the dispute surrounding an order allowing him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International case under house arrest.
The matter was listed before High Court judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin at the Kuala Lumpur High Court Criminal Court 5 at 2.30pm today.
The Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) has applied to review the November 6 discharge order and obtain a fresh order consistent with the conditional pardon granted to Najib by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim, on September 18.
Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar reportedly confirmed the application to NST.

Title: Health inflation in Malaysia more than doubles to 3pc in 2025, says Stats Dept
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 10 — Health Inflation increased 3.0 per cent in 2025 as compared to 1.3 per cent in 2024, according to the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM).
It said the increase was driven by the Health Services category, which recorded a significant rise of 4.4 per cent as compared to 0.9 per cent in 2024, which contributed by the Insurance connected with health expenditure class that increased by 9.1 per cent in 2025 (2024: 0.0%).
The Medicine category represents the largest weight, accounting for 38.9 per cent in Health Price Index (HPI), recorded an increase of 2.8 per cent in 2025, compared with 2.2 per cent in the previous year.
“The increase was driven by the Medicines expenditure class, which includes the Medicines, vaccines & other pharmaceutical preparations and Herbal medicines & homeopathic products expenditure subclasses.
“Both subclasses recorded increases of 4.5 per cent in 2025 as compared to 2.2 per cent and 0.7 per cent in 2024, respectively,” DOSM said in a statement accompanying the Annual Health Price Index 2025 report released today.
This report provides the HPI (2022=100) and Health Inflation, which takes into account both treatment and prevention healthcare aspects comprising three categories, namely Medicine, Medical Devices and Health Services at the national level.
DOSM released the HPI for the first time, presenting detailed findings following the release of the Preliminary Report on Malaysia Health Price Index 2025 in July 2026. The statistics measure changes in the prices of healthcare-related goods and services purchased by households.
The development of the HPI is an initiative by DOSM, in collaboration with relevant health-related agencies from both the public and private sectors and through the integration of data from various sources.
Meanwhile, the department said the Medical Devices category also increased 1.1 per cent (2024: 0.6 per cent), driven by the Medical products expenditure class, 1.3 per cent (2024: 0.6 per cent).
The increase was contributed by the Medical diagnostic products expenditure subclass, which recorded an increase of 1.6 per cent, as compared to 0.3 per cent in 2024.
The compilation of Malaysia HPI incorporates health-related components from three groups in the Consumer Price Index (CPI), namely the Health group, the Insurance and Financial Services group and the Personal Care, Social Protection and Miscellaneous Goods and Services group.
The HPI complements the indicators of health-related inflation and helps the government, stakeholders and the public identify trends in the healthcare cost movements, thereby supporting more effective planning, implementation and monitoring in the healthcare sector. — Bernama

Title: MetMalaysia issues storm warning for parts of Selangor, Johor, KL and six other states until 5pm today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected in parts of 10 states and Kuala Lumpur until 5pm today, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said.
In a warning issued at 12.45pm, the department said the affected areas include the whole of Perlis, as well as Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap and Pokok Sena in Kedah.
In Pahang, the warning covers Maran, Bera, Temerloh and Bentong, while in Selangor it involves Gombak, Hulu Langat, Petaling and Hulu Selangor.
The warning also covers Kuala Lumpur, Jelebu in Negeri Sembilan, and Pontian, Johor Baru, Kulai and Mersing in Johor.
In Sarawak, the affected areas are Limbang and Marudi in Miri, while in Sabah they include Tawau, Pensiangan and Tambunan in the Interior Division, as well as the West Coast Division.
MetMalaysia said thunderstorm warnings are issued when there are signs of thunderstorms with rainfall intensity exceeding 20mm per hour, either occurring or expected to occur for more than an hour.
It said such warnings were short-term alerts valid for no more than six hours for each issuance.

Title: ITU PP-26: Malaysia developing national plan for post-quantum cryptography, says Fahmi
Article:
DOHA, Nov 10 — Malaysia is developing a national plan to transition its critical information infrastructure to post-quantum cryptography, as part of efforts to strengthen cybersecurity and prepare the country for emerging threats posed by quantum computing.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said he had instructed the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) to engage with the National Security Council (MKN), National Cyber Security Agency (NACSA) and telecommunications operators to establish a shared research and development (R&D) testbed.
He said the initiative would allow relevant stakeholders to jointly test solutions and accelerate the transition to quantum-resistant cryptography in a secure and coordinated manner.
“As quantum communications develop, governments and industry players must build trust and interoperability through common standards, equipment testing and a phased transition to quantum-resistant cryptography, without disrupting essential services.
“Malaysia is developing a national plan to move critical information infrastructure to post-quantum cryptography. I have asked MCMC to engage NSC, NACSA and telecommunications operators on a shared R&D testbed.
“This would let us test solutions together, and accelerate the transition securely,” he said when delivering Malaysia's policy statement at the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Plenipotentiary Conference 2026 (PP-26), here, yesterday.
On Sunday, Fahmi said that he had asked MCMC to hold discussions with the NSC, NACSA and telecommunications companies to explore potential collaboration, to facilitate a faster and more secure transition to quantum-resistant technologies in Malaysia.
Quantum migration refers to the process of upgrading existing digital security systems to adopt quantum-resistant encryption technologies, designed to protect data against potential threats from future quantum computers.
Fahmi is currently in Doha to lead the Malaysian delegation to ITU PP-26, which runs from November 6 to 11.
He is accompanied by Communications Ministry deputy secretary-general (Telecommunications Infrastructure), Mano Verabathran.
The Malaysian delegation also includes representatives from the MCMC and telecommunications companies, including Telekom Malaysia (TM), CelcomDigi, Maxis and U Mobile.As a specialised agency of the United Nations (UN) responsible for digital technologies, the ITU plays a key role in international telecommunications cooperation, radio spectrum coordination and efforts to bridge the global digital divide. — Bernama

Title: Police probe boy’s fall after clinging to moving vehicle near Nilai toll plaza
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 10 — Police are investigating an incident involving a boy who fell onto the road after clinging to the rear door of a moving vehicle, as seen in a video that went viral on social media, believed to have occurred near the Nilai toll plaza here.
Nilai police chief Supt Johari Yahya said police received a report on the circulation of the one-minute video at 11.02pm yesterday.
He said the footage was believed to have been recorded by a dashboard camera in another vehicle, whose owner, a woman, had been contacted to provide a statement and the original recording of the incident.
However, police have yet to receive any response from her.
“Based on a statement uploaded by the woman, the boy’s family members are believed to have turned back on foot to retrieve him, as the location of the incident was far from the nearest U-turn,” he said in a statement here today.
Johari said police were now working to verify the information, including recording a statement from the dashboard camera owner and tracing the boy and his family members to assist in the investigation.
The case is being investigated under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001.
Members of the public with information on the incident are urged to contact the Nilai district police headquarters (IPD) Operations Room at 06-790 4222 or any nearby police station. — Bernama

Title: Court to hear AGC application for fresh order to facilitate Najib's house arrest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — The High Court in Kuala Lumpur is expected to have a hearing this afternoon the Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) application to correct a court order or issue a fresh court order to enable former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest.
When contacted today, Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar confirmed to
Malay Mail t
hat there would be a court hearing this afternoon for the AGC’s “Rectification Application”.
Based on the court’s online filing system, the application is expected to be heard before High Court judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin at 2.30pm.
Earlier today, Dusuki confirmed to
Malay Mail
that the AGC had asked the courts to issue a new court order for the house arrest.
“AGC has filed an application at the High Court in Kuala Lumpur today, Nov 10, 2026 (Tuesday) to review and rescrutinise the Order of Discharge issued on November 6, 2026 and for a new Order of Discharge so that it is in line with the order to pardon granted by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on September 18, 2026,” he told Malay Mail in a brief text message.
Yesterday, local daily Berita Harian reported Dusuki as saying the High Court in Kuala Lumpur’s Order of Discharge for Najib contained obvious errors or defects.
Najib is currently still at Kajang Prison, as the Attorney General’s Chambers has previously highlighted the need to clarify legal matters related to Najib’s house arrest.

Title: Penang includes mitigation plans at flood hotspots under 2040 structure plan
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 10 — Penang’s draft Structure Plan 2040 includes proposals to upgrade flood hotspots and install pumps in certain areas, state Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye said today.
He said the proposed measures included the installation of flood mitigation infrastructure at selected locations.
“I believe that under the Structure Plan 2040, we also have plans to look at hotspot areas where upgrades have been proposed.
“These include the installation of screw pumps and submersible pumps in certain areas,” he told reporters after he was asked about the state’s plans to mitigate flooding, including recent flooding in an industrial area in Bayan Lepas.
He also said state exco Zairil Khir Johari has several flood mitigation projects in his portfolio to resolve flooding in hotspots in the state.
Asked whether uneven urban planning could be contributing to flash floods, H’ng said he believed most developments on both the island and mainland complied with the conditions of their planning permission.
He added that these projects have complied with strict conditions before obtaining approvals for earthworks and building plans.
He said developers needed to meet the stipulated conditions to obtain a Certificate of Completion and Compliance (CCC).
“If they are found to have breached the conditions, the local authorities have the right to withhold permission for their architects to issue the CCC,” he said.
H’ng said local authorities had the right to act if developers were found not to have complied with the conditions.

Title: Residents of four affected homes in Paya Terubong still not allowed to return home as DOSH awaits mitigation plan
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 10 — The residents of four houses affected by the fatal landslide in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, have yet to be allowed to return home, state Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye said today.
He said the Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) is still waiting for the developer’s civil engineer, Aptitute Consulting Engineers Sdn Bhd, to submit full documentations and a formal application to carry out mitigation and repair works at the collapsed slope.
“The documents and application are expected to be submitted to DOSH tomorrow for its consideration,” he told a press conference today.
He said the developer’s consultants, including its geotechnical and civil engineers, were asked to submit a mitigation plan and an application to DOSH after meeting with the organisation.
“Only then can DOSH issue approval to the developer to carry out the mitigation works. For the time being, the residents of four units are still not allowed to return to their homes,” he said.
He said DOSH had requested a landslide report from the developer’s geotechnical engineer, WYA Consulting Engineers Sdn Bhd, and the company had submitted the report on November 5.
“For the time being, the residents of four units are still not allowed to return to their homes,” he added.
The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) had previously declared four houses — numbered 1, 3, 5 and 7 — unsafe for occupation, while two others, numbered 9 and 11, were cleared for reoccupation.
In the October 25 landslide, 73-year-old doctor Wong Kar Lin was killed after he was buried in the landslide, which also affected his home.
His wife, Chang Mei Nuo, 68, and mother-in-law, Wong Poh Lim, who is in her 80s, managed to escape.
H’ng had previously said the state would focus on DOSH’s investigation before discussing calls by non-governmental organisations for a state commission of inquiry into the tragedy.

Title: AG: Courts asked to issue new house arrest order for Najib
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — The Attorney-General’s Chambers has asked the courts to issue a new order for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest in line with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong’s September pardon, the attorney general said today.
When contacted today, Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar confirmed the application for a new order was filed with the courts today.
“AGC has filed an application at the High Court in Kuala Lumpur today, Nov 10, 2026 (Tuesday) to review and rescrutinise the Order of Discharge issued on November 6, 2026 and for a new Order of Discharge so that it is in line with the order to pardon granted by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on September 18, 2026,” he told
Malay Mail i
n a brief text message.
Dusuki confirmed that this application is known as a rectification application.
Yesterday, local daily
Berita Harian
reported Dusuki as saying the High Court in Kuala Lumpur's Order of Discharge for Najib contained obvious errors or defects.
Najib is currently still at Kajang Prison, as the Attorney General's Chambers has previously highlighted the need to clarify legal matters related to Najib's house arrest.
In 2024, a royal pardon over Najib’s SRC International case resulted in the reduction of his 12-year jail term to six years, and his RM210 million fine to RM50 million.
On September 18, Najib was given a conditional pardon in his SRC International case, which allowed him to serve the rest of his jail term under house arrest until August 23, 2028, if he pays the RM50 million fine.
On November 6, Umno paid the RM50 million fine on Najib's behalf, which resulted in the High Court in Kuala Lumpur issuing an Order of Discharge to enable Najib's house arrest to take place.
Since then, the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) had explained it was not disputing or setting aside the Agong's conditional pardon order for Najib's house arrest.
The AGC said there needs to be a court decision to clear uncertainties on whether the RM50 million payment meant the SRC International sentence had been fully resolved or if Najib still had to serve the remaining jail term on house arrest.
The AGC said this is because it could impact when Najib has to start serving his separate jail term in the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) case.
In Najib's 1MDB case, the High Court had in December 2025 ordered him to start serving his 15-year jail term after the end of his SRC International jail term.
Najib is currently appealing his 1MDB conviction and sentence, and the High Court had on October 14 rejected his bid to stay or to pause the carrying out of the 1MDB sentence.

Title: Floods, storm and landslide leave 422 evacuees at relief centres in Perak, Selangor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — A total of 422 evacuees from 119 families remain at temporary relief centres (PPS) in Perak and Selangor as of this morning.
In Perak, the State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) Secretariat said the number of flood evacuees had dropped to 410 people from 114 families, compared with 419 people from 124 families last night.
It said all evacuees were currently housed at three PPS in two districts.
“Larut, Matang and Selama was the latest district to be affected by flooding, with 39 people from eight families evacuated to the PPS at Surau Kampung Simpang Halt last night.
“In Hilir Perak, 238 flood evacuees from 69 families are housed at the Teluk Intan Municipal Council (MPTI) Rest House Hall, while another 133 from 37 families are taking shelter at the MPTI Langkap Hall,” the secretariat said in a statement.
Meanwhile, in Selangor, 12 storm victims from three families remain at the PPS at Dewan Sri Bernam in Sabak Bernam, according to the Social Welfare Department's (JKM) InfoBencana portal.
Another 20 people from five families displaced by a landslide in Gombak on October 29 remain at the PPS at Balai Raya Kampung Kenanga. — Bernama

Title: DAP committed to nation-building regardless of govt or opposition role, says veep Teo Nie Ching
Article:
KULAI, Nov 10 — The DAP wants to continue playing its role as a nation-building party, regardless of whether it is in government or the opposition, by championing transparent, fair and sustainable policies, said its vice-president Teo Nie Ching.
Teo, who is also deputy communications minister, said the principle formed the basis of DAP’s struggle to ensure Malaysia continued to develop as a nation with a sustainable governance system, while prioritising the interests and welfare of the people.
“Regardless of whether we are in the opposition or in government, we want to be a nation builder.
“… we want to develop our country together, and that is why we want to ensure that we can make Malaysia a country with a sustainable system,” she said in an exclusive interview with Bernama recently.
The Wanita DAP chief said the party’s contribution to nation-building was not confined to economic and physical development, but also included efforts to strengthen inclusive and fair policies, including taking into account the needs of women and children.
Commenting on DAP’s participation in the Madani Government, Teo said its position provided the party with an opportunity to translate its principles into policies and action through direct involvement in the country’s administration.
The Kulai MP said the priority was to ensure that the policies it championed could be implemented transparently and benefit the people, thereby contributing to the country’s long-term development.
“Our intention is to ensure that we can contribute to nation-building by ensuring that we have policies that are more open and transparent,” she said.
Asked about DAP’s approach ahead of the 16th General Election, Teo said the party left it to the people to make their own assessment, but efforts to win over voters should be based on its achievements and track record during its time in government.
She cited the establishment of the Malaysian Media Council (MMM), which was among the reform agendas championed by the party for more than 50 years before being realised through the passage of the Malaysian Media Council Act under the Madani Government.
“Malaysia now has the MMM, chaired by a former Federal Court judge, demonstrating the efforts to realise the institutional reform agenda under the Madani Government.
“In addition, Pakatan Harapan has also championed the proposal to limit the Prime Minister’s term of office, with Penang becoming the first state to amend its state constitution to limit the Chief Minister’s tenure to 10 years. The agenda was subsequently brought to the federal government level, with the hope that the proposal would be passed in the Dewan Rakyat,” she said.
Touching on the challenges of implementing policies while in government, Teo said not all decisions received the support of every party, particularly when the interests of certain groups were involved.
She said this was among the challenges faced by parties in government, but their track record in implementing policies should serve as evidence to the people of the efforts undertaken.
“I believe that being in government does come with its pros and cons. The cons are quite obvious because not all policies will be supported by everyone.
“...when we, for example, decided to raise the minimum wage to RM2,000, there are business people and employers who disagree with that direction. But I think what is most important is that we show voters our track record so that they will be willing to give DAP a chance,” she said. — Bernama
